title: Localization preserves projective dimension and finite global dimension
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $S\subseteq R$ a multiplicative subset, $S^{-1}R$ the ring of fractions and, for an $R$-module $M$, $S^{-1}M$ the $S^{-1}R$-module of fractions $m/s$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]; let $n\ge0$. (1) If $M$ has a projective resolution of length $\le n$ over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-global-dimension], that is, an exact sequence $0\to P_n\to\dots\to P_0\to M\to0$ with every $P_i$ a projective $R$-module [def-weil-pbc-projective-module], then $S^{-1}M$ has a projective resolution of length $\le n$ over $S^{-1}R$. (2) If $R$ has global dimension $\le n$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-global-dimension], then $S^{-1}R$ has global dimension $\le n$; in particular, if $R$ has finite global dimension then so has $S^{-1}R$, with $\operatorname{gl.dim}S^{-1}R\le\operatorname{gl.dim}R$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00O8 (lemma-localize-finite-gl-dim, line 26881), with its proof (localization is exact, Proposition 00CS; $S^{-1}P$ projective for $P$ projective, Lemma 05A3 ascend-properties-modules; $M'=S^{-1}M'$ for an $S^{-1}R$-module $M'$)

proof.text: Localizing the resolution gives an exact sequence. Let $0\to P_n\xrightarrow{d_n}P_{n-1}\to\dots\to P_0\xrightarrow{d_0}M\to0$ be a projective resolution of $M$ of length $\le n$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-global-dimension]; it is exact at every inner term [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence]. Apply $S^{-1}$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization] to every module and map, obtaining $0\to S^{-1}P_n\xrightarrow{S^{-1}d_n}\dots\to S^{-1}P_0\xrightarrow{S^{-1}d_0}S^{-1}M\to0$; the maps $S^{-1}d_i:p/s\mapsto d_i(p)/s$ are $S^{-1}R$-linear, since $S^{-1}d_i((a/t)(p/s))=d_i(ap)/(ts)=(a/t)\,(d_i(p)/s)$, and $S^{-1}0=0$. Each piece of three consecutive terms $X\xrightarrow{u}Y\xrightarrow{v}Z$ of the original sequence (including $0\to P_n\to P_{n-1}$ and $P_0\to M\to0$) is exact, so by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-exact] the localized piece $S^{-1}X\to S^{-1}Y\to S^{-1}Z$ is exact. Hence the localized sequence is exact at every term: $S^{-1}d_n$ is injective, $S^{-1}d_0$ is surjective, and $\ker S^{-1}d_{i}=\operatorname{im}S^{-1}d_{i+1}$ for $0\le i<n$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00O8 (lemma-localize-finite-gl-dim, line 26881), proof, first sentence ('As localization is exact, see Proposition 00CS')

proof.text: Proof of (1). Each $P_i$ is a projective $R$-module [def-weil-pbc-projective-module], so $S^{-1}P_i$ is a projective $S^{-1}R$-module by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-projective]. Together with Step 1, $0\to S^{-1}P_n\to\dots\to S^{-1}P_0\to S^{-1}M\to0$ is an exact sequence of $S^{-1}R$-modules with projective terms $S^{-1}P_i$, i.e. a projective resolution of $S^{-1}M$ of length $\le n$ over $S^{-1}R$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-global-dimension]. This is (1).

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00O8 (lemma-localize-finite-gl-dim, line 26881), proof, first sentence ('as each $S^{-1}P_i$ is a projective $S^{-1}R$-module, see Lemma 05A3 ... This proves (1)')

proof.text: Proof of (2), first assertion. Assume every $R$-module has a projective resolution of length $\le n$. Let $M'$ be any $S^{-1}R$-module and regard it as an $R$-module through $R\to S^{-1}R$, $r\mapsto r/1$. By hypothesis $M'$ has a projective resolution $0\to P_n\to\dots\to P_0\xrightarrow{\varepsilon}M'\to0$ over $R$, so by (1) (Step 2) $0\to S^{-1}P_n\to\dots\to S^{-1}P_0\xrightarrow{S^{-1}\varepsilon}S^{-1}M'\to0$ is a projective resolution of length $\le n$ over $S^{-1}R$. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-over-localization] the map $\varphi:S^{-1}M'\to M'$, $m/s\mapsto(1/s)m$, is an isomorphism of $S^{-1}R$-modules. Replacing the last map $S^{-1}\varepsilon$ by $\varphi\circ S^{-1}\varepsilon:S^{-1}P_0\to M'$ keeps the sequence exact (its kernel is $\ker S^{-1}\varepsilon$ and it is surjective, as $\varphi$ is bijective), so $0\to S^{-1}P_n\to\dots\to S^{-1}P_0\to M'\to0$ is a projective resolution of $M'$ of length $\le n$ over $S^{-1}R$. As $M'$ was arbitrary, $S^{-1}R$ has global dimension $\le n$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-global-dimension].

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00O8 (lemma-localize-finite-gl-dim, line 26881), proof, second paragraph ('Let $M'$ be an $S^{-1}R$-module. Note that $M' = S^{-1}M'$. Hence we see that (2) follows from (1).')

proof.text: Proof of (2), 'in particular'. If $R$ has finite global dimension $d=\operatorname{gl.dim}R$, then $R$ has global dimension $\le d$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-global-dimension], so by Step 3 with $n=d$ every $S^{-1}R$-module has a projective resolution of length $\le d$: $S^{-1}R$ has finite global dimension, and its global dimension, the least $n'$ such that every $S^{-1}R$-module has a projective resolution of length $\le n'$, is $\le d$.

lean.statement: theorem localization_preserves_projective_and_global_dimension (R : Type u) [CommRing R] (S : Submonoid R) (n : ℕ) : (∀ M : ModuleCat.{max u v} R, ModuleCat.HasProjectiveResolutionLE M n → ModuleCat.HasProjectiveResolutionLE (ModuleCat.of (Localization S) (LocalizedModule S M)) n) ∧ (HasGlobalDimensionLE.{u, max u v} R n → HasGlobalDimensionLE.{u, max u v} (Localization S) n) ∧ (∀ h : HasFiniteGlobalDimension.{u, max u v} R, ∃ hS : HasFiniteGlobalDimension.{u, max u v} (Localization S), globalDimension.{u, max u v} (Localization S) hS ≤ globalDimension.{u, max u v} R h)
